provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Numbers 21 to 30
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to count numbers to 30.
The pupils should be able to write numbers from 21 to 30.
The pupils should be able to identify tens and ones.

Introduction:
We have learned numbers to 20. Today we learn numbers to 30.
We will use our fingers and counters to count.

Content:
Numbers from 21 to 30.
21 is two tens and one one.
22 is two tens and two ones.
We can count using our fingers.
We can use stones to show tens and ones.

Class activity:
Pupils will count objects in the classroom.
Each pupil will count 25 sticks.

Evaluation questions:
Count from 21 to 30.
Write the number after 25.
How many tens are in 30?

Summary:
We have learned numbers to 30.
We know how to count and write them.

topics.title: Numbers 31 to 40
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to count numbers to 40.
The pupils should be able to write numbers from 31 to 40.
The pupils should be able to fill the missing numbers.

Introduction:
We learned numbers to 30 last week.
Today we will learn numbers to 40.

Content:
Numbers from 31 to 40.
31 is three tens and one one.
35 is three tens and five ones.
We can fill gaps in number lines.
Example: 32, __, 34, 35, __.

Class activity:
Pupils will fill missing numbers on worksheets.
They will work in pairs to check answers.

Evaluation questions:
Count from 31 to 40.
Write the number before 38.
Fill the gap: 36, __, 38.

Summary:
We have learned numbers to 40.
We can now fill missing numbers.

topics.title: Numbers 41 to 50
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to count numbers to 50.
The pupils should be able to write numbers from 41 to 50.
The pupils should be able to identify tens and ones.

Introduction:
We have learned numbers to 40.
Today we will learn numbers to 50.

Content:
Numbers from 41 to 50.
41 is four tens and one one.
45 is four tens and five ones.
We can group objects into tens and ones.
Example: 4 groups of ten and 5 ones make 45.

Class activity:
Pupils will make groups of ten with bottle caps.
They will show numbers with their groups.

Evaluation questions:
Count from 41 to 50.
Write the number after 47.
How many tens are in 50?

Summary:
We have learned numbers to 50.
We know tens and ones in these numbers.

topics.title: Addition of numbers to 20
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to add numbers to 20.
The pupils should be able to write addition sums.
The pupils should be able to solve simple addition problems.

Introduction:
We have learned numbers to 50.
Today we will learn how to add small numbers.

Content:
Adding means putting numbers together.
We can use counters to add.
Example: 5 + 3 = 8.
We count all counters together.
We write + for add and = for equals.

Class activity:
Pupils will use counters to add numbers.
They will work in pairs to solve 5 + 4.

Evaluation questions:
What is 3 + 5?
Write 4 + 2 = .
Solve 6 + 1 = .

Summary:
We have learned how to add numbers to 20.
We can use counters to help us.

topics.title: Subtraction from numbers to 20
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to subtract numbers from 20.
The pupils should be able to write subtraction sums.
The pupils should be able to solve simple subtraction problems.

Introduction:
We learned how to add numbers last week.
Today we will learn how to take away numbers.

Content:
Subtract means to take away.
We can use counters to subtract.
Example: 8 - 3 = 5.
We take away counters and count what is left.
We write - for take away and = for equals.

Class activity:
Pupils will use counters to subtract numbers.
They will work in groups to solve 10 - 4.

Evaluation questions:
What is 9 - 4?
Write 7 - 2 = .
Solve 10 - 5 = .

Summary:
We have learned how to subtract numbers.
We can use counters to help us.

topics.title: Money: naira and kobo
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify naira coins and notes.
The pupils should be able to count small amounts of money.
The pupils should be able to do simple shopping play.

Introduction:
We have learned numbers and addition.
Today we will learn about money in Nigeria.

Content:
We use naira and kobo in Nigeria.
Naira is written as N.
Kobo is written as k.
100 kobo = 1 naira.
We have coins for 10k, 25k, 50k.
We have notes for N1, N5, N10, N20, N50, N100, N200, N500, N1000.

Class activity:
Pupils will play shop with toy money.
Some pupils will be shopkeepers and others will buy things.

Evaluation questions:
What is 10k + 10k?
Which coin is the biggest?
How much is 50k + 50k?

Summary:
We have learned about naira and kobo.
We can count small amounts of money.

topics.title: Length: long and short
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to compare objects by length.
The pupils should be able to order objects from short to long.
The pupils should be able to identify long and short things.

Introduction:
We have learned about money.
Today we will learn about long and short things.

Content:
Length means how long or short something is.
We compare things to see which is longer or shorter.
Example: a pencil is short, a ruler is long.
We can order things by length.
Shortest to longest: pencil, book, table.

Class activity:
Pupils will collect objects from the classroom.
They will order their objects from shortest to longest.

Evaluation questions:
Which is longer, a pen or a book?
Order these from short to long: book, pencil, ruler.
Name something longer than your hand.

Summary:
We have learned about long and short.
We can compare and order objects by length.

topics.title: Weight: heavy and light
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to compare objects by weight.
The pupils should be able to identify heavy and light objects.
The pupils should be able to sort objects by weight.

Introduction:
We learned about long and short last week.
Today we will learn about heavy and light things.

Content:
Weight means how heavy or light something is.
We can feel weight by carrying things.
Example: a stone is heavy, a feather is light.
We can sort things into heavy and light.
Heavy things are hard to carry.
Light things are easy to carry.

Class activity:
Pupils will carry different objects.
They will sort them into heavy and light piles.

Evaluation questions:
Which is heavier, a book or a pencil?
Sort these: stone, feather, book, paper.
Name something light that you can carry easily.

Summary:
We have learned about heavy and light.
We can compare and sort objects by weight.

topics.title: Time: day and night
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify day and night.
The pupils should be able to name activities done in morning and evening.
The pupils should be able to sequence daily activities.

Introduction:
We have learned about heavy and light.
Today we will learn about time in a day.

Content:
A day has morning, afternoon and night.
We wake up in the morning.
We eat lunch in the afternoon.
We sleep at night.
Different activities happen at different times.
Example: we go to school in the morning.

Class activity:
Pupils will draw pictures of morning and evening activities.
They will make a chart of their daily routine.

Evaluation questions:
What do you do in the morning?
What happens at night?
When do you eat your lunch?

Summary:
We have learned about day and night.
We know activities for different times.

topics.title: Revision and assessment
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to count numbers to 50.
The pupils should be able to add and subtract small numbers.
The pupils should be able to identify long, short, heavy, light, day and night.

Introduction:
Today we will revise what we learned this term.
We will play games to remember our lessons.

Content:
We will count numbers to 50.
We will practice addition and subtraction.
We will review money, length, weight and time.
Example: What is 5 + 3?
Which is longer, a book or a pencil?
What happens at night?

Class activity:
Pupils will play math games in teams.
They will answer questions to earn points.

Evaluation questions:
Count from 31 to 40.
What is 10 - 4?
Sort these: book, feather, stone, paper.
What do you do in the morning?

Summary:
We have revised all our topics this term.
We are ready for our exam.
